_comment: WRITTEN BEFORE THE TOOL WAS RUN ON THIS FIXTURE. Every `expect` below is derived from reading the source, not from output. If a row later needs changing, append a dated note saying why — never edit one to match a result.
_measures: CAPABILITY and PRECISION, not a rate. n=4 positives cannot estimate real-world recall; what it can establish is whether each documented cross-stack mechanism resolves at all, and whether the three name-matching traps are avoided. Real-world recall needs hand-verified pairs in a real repo, which this does not substitute for.

positives.why: createWorkOrder INSERTs into work_orders; WorkOrderSync.sync SELECTs from it. No import, no call edge, different languages — the table is the only link. A scheduler invokes the Java side, so it has zero in-repo callers and looks isolated to a call graph.
InvoicePoster INSERTs invoices; InvoiceReport reads Invoice via ActiveRecord. Neither language can see the other, and the ORM never spells the table name in SQL — it is inferred from the model name.
The panel does $http.get("/api/technicians"); the controller serves @GetMapping("/api/technicians"). The shared route literal is the entire boundary.

Four languages read the same environment variable and NOTHING links them -- no import, no call, no table, no route. Redefine what the value means on one side and the other three silently change behaviour. Deliberately four accessor IDIOMS as well as four languages (process.env.X dotted, System.getenv("X"), ENV["X"], os.environ.get("X")), because an adapter is only as multi-language as the idioms it was tested on.
positives.addedNote: 2026-07-30: was a declared GAP -- there was no config-key adapter at all, which this benchmark found on its first run. Adapter added; the row now expects three counterparts across three other languages rather than one.

positives.why: JAX-RS declares this route in TWO annotations: @Path on the class and @Path on the method. Neither half matches the client's composed `/{realm}/partial-export`, so a scanner that reads only the method annotation finds nothing — and one that reads only literals never sees `partial-export` at all, because it is a single segment with no slash. Verified on the real keycloak repo: 19 of 25 route keys on the admin client had NO counterpart, including partial-export, which exists on both sides (RealmAdminResource.java:1363).

decoys.why: closeWorkOrder writes work_orders.status; TechnicianReport reads technicians.status. Identical COLUMN name, unrelated tables. This is the trap a column-grained matcher falls into, and it is why the shape's documented grain is the TABLE.
Help.tsx mentions work_orders twice in user-facing text and touches no database. `rg work_orders` matches it. A resolved access must not.
audit_log is written and read inside one file, so there is no other side. Reporting the file against itself would be a false discovery dressed as a cross-stack finding.

SOLO_ONLY_FLAG is read here and nowhere else. A config key is the one SYMMETRIC kind -- other_side unions producers and consumers so that reader-to-reader pairs resolve -- so this is the case where that union could make a file its own counterpart. It must report nothing.

Composed paths /{realm}/client-registration-policy/providers and /admin/policies/providers/{id} share the literal segment `providers` and nothing else. Seam linked EXACTLY this pair on real keycloak. This decoy exists so that widening route matching to fix the split-path miss cannot be paid for with invented edges — the failure mode a looser matcher produces.
